symptom: An ambient Array.prototype numeric-index setter intercepted ordinary out[i] assignment during bounded graph/policy snapshots and anchor accumulation. In a local synthetic 19-element reproduction, the setter changed a later caller-owned element before it was copied. For a policy with an initially invalid later anchor, the setter could repair the original anchor and install the intercepted array index, allowing a later metadata-consistent verdict. This is not independent proof or scoring authority.
lesson: Descriptor-only reads of caller inputs are insufficient if the detached output is populated by ordinary array index assignment: inherited setters on the output prototype can run code and mutate later source fields. The same risk exists when accumulating validated anchors after a snapshot.
guardrail: Use Object.defineProperty with an own enumerable writable configurable numeric data property when building detached arrays and validated anchor lists. Negative tests should install a reversible high-index Array.prototype setter that repairs a later invalid field, verify the setter is never invoked, and confirm the original invalid data remains denied. Preserve untrusted/non-scoring flags; do not infer atomicity against arbitrary cross-input Proxies.
